answer: Sybil resistance by quadratic influence: an agent voting weight grows only as the square root of its bonded stake, so splitting one deposit across a swarm of fresh identities that wander in from nowhere buys strictly less total weight than keeping it whole. An attacker who spawns a comet-tail of look-alike accounts still pays full capital for each, yet collects sharply diminishing returns, turning the economics of a sybil fleet into a losing fable rather than a cheap exploit.
